changelog: A MAC-FOCUSED BUILD — everything here is about how the game behaves on a Mac; the Windows and Android builds follow separately. THE BATTLEFIELD NOW WORKS LIKE A CAMERA. Pinch on the trackpad to zoom, two fingers to pan, and 0 to snap back to the whole board. Zooming holds the point under your cursor instead of jumping to the middle, and panning stops at the edge of the table rather than drifting off into nothing — the Mac could not zoom at all before this. THE BOARD FITS THE WINDOW AGAIN: a battle opens with the whole battlefield visible and nothing to scroll to, and scrolling only appears once you zoom in, which is what it was always meant to do. THE REPLAY FOLLOWS THE FIGHT — when a shot is fired at ground you can see but are not looking at, the camera moves there first and then plays it, so you watch the hit land instead of finding the aftermath; anything in fog is left alone. FIXED: the sluggishness during play; commander portraits and their doctrine text vanishing from the Generals page after scrolling; Settings opening behind the Generals panel; the top bar overlapping itself and slicing labels in half in a smaller window; the menu title flickering as the pointer crossed the buttons; and buttons that responded four different ways to a hover now all behaving the same. Still universal and still notarized: one download runs natively on Intel and Apple Silicon, and opens with no Gatekeeper warning.
